newsitem.title: USA: Feed Grains Council sees 9.49 bln bu US corn crop.
newsitem.headline: Feed Grains Council sees 9.49 bln bu US corn crop.

text.p: U.S. corn production will rise modestly to 9.490 billion bushels this year, the U.S. Feed Grains Council said Tuesday, projecting rapid growth in output and usage of American grains in the coming decade.

The council also projected a soybean crop of 2.382 billion bushels, wheat at 2.449 billion bushels, sorghum at 610 million bushels, barley at 377 million bushels and oats at 168 million. The cotton harvest would be 17.36 million bales.
The farm-gate corn price in 1997/98 would be $2.45 a bushel, soybeans $6.15 and wheat $3.59, all down from this season.

According to the forecast, U.S. corn acreage will rise 1.1 percent, to 80.7 million acres (30 million hectares) this year and output by 2.4 percent. Exports would leap seven percent to 2.092 billion bushels (52.88 million tonnes).
"This implies a modest 8.3 million tonne, or 32.8 percent, increase in stocks and a season average price of about $2.45 per bushel, a level exceeded only twice since 1984," it said.
The average corn price for 1996/97 would be $2.74.
When sorghum, barley and oats were added, feed (coarse) grain area would drop slightly but production would be stable due to higher yields, it said.
